act_title: Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (as amended by 2018 Act)
marginal_heading: Offence Relating to Public Servant Being Bribed
text: Any public servant who obtains or accepts or attempts to obtain from any person, an undue advantage, with the intention to perform or cause performance of public duty improperly or dishonestly, or to forbear performance of such duty, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.

marginal_heading: Criminal Misconduct by a Public Servant & Disproportionate Assets
text: A public servant commits the offence of criminal misconduct if he dishonestly or fraudulently misappropriates or otherwise converts for his own use any property entrusted to him or under his control, or if he intentionally enriches himself illicitly during the period of his office. If a public servant cannot satisfactorily account for pecuniary resources or property disproportionate to his known sources of income, he shall be punishable with imprisonment not less than four years up to ten years.

marginal_heading: Prior Approval for Inquiry, Inquiry or Investigation (Protection for Official Decisions)
text: No police officer shall conduct any inquiry or inquiry or investigation into any offence alleged to have been committed by a public servant under this Act, where the alleged offence is relatable to any recommendation made or decision taken by such public servant in discharge of his official functions or duties, without the previous approval of the competent authority, except in cases involving arrest on the spot on the charge of accepting or attempting to accept any undue advantage.

act_title: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (NDPS)
marginal_heading: Punishment for Contravention in Relation to Cannabis Plant and Cannabis (Charas, Ganja)
citation: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, Sec. 20
text: Whoever contravenes any provision of this Act or any rule or order made or condition of licence granted thereunder in relation to cannabis shall be punishable: (i) small quantity (up to 1kg Ganja, 100g Charas): rigorous imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to ₹10,000, or both; (ii) intermediate quantity: rigorous imprisonment up to ten years and fine up to ₹1,00,000; (iii) commercial quantity (20kg Ganja, 1kg Charas): rigorous imprisonment not less than ten years extending to twenty years, and fine not less than ₹1,00,000 extending to ₹2,00,000.

act_title: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (NDPS)
marginal_heading: Offences to be Cognizable and Non-Bailable (Twin Conditions for Bail)
citation: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, Sec. 37
text: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure / BNSS, every offence punishable under this Act shall be cognizable and non-bailable. For offences involving commercial quantity, bail shall not be granted unless: (i) the Public Prosecutor has been given an opportunity to oppose the application; and (ii) where the Public Prosecutor opposes, the court is satisfied that there are reasonable grounds for believing that the accused is not guilty of such offence and that he is not likely to commit any offence while on bail.

act_title: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (NDPS)
marginal_heading: Conditions Under Which Search of Persons Shall Be Conducted (Gazetted Officer / Magistrate)
citation: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, Sec. 50
text: When any officer duly authorized is about to search any person under the provisions of Section 41, 42 or 43, he shall, if such person so requires, take such person without unnecessary delay to the nearest Gazetted Officer of any of the departments mentioned in Section 42 or to the nearest Magistrate. Failure to apprise the suspect of this mandatory statutory right invalidates the recovery of contraband from the person (State of Punjab v. Baldev Singh / Vijaysinh Chandubha Jadeja).

act_title: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO)
citation: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Sec. 4
text: Whoever commits penetrative sexual assault on a child shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. Where penetrative sexual assault is committed on a child below sixteen years of age, the punishment shall be rigorous imprisonment for a term not less than twenty years up to life, or death.

act_title: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO)
citation: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Sec. 19
text: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure / BNSS, any person (including the child, medical practitioner, teacher, or relative) who has apprehension that an offence under this Act has been committed shall provide such information to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or the local police. Section 21 penalizes failure to report or record an offence with imprisonment up to six months or fine or both.

act_title: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO)
marginal_heading: Presumption as to Certain Offences (Reverse Burden of Proof)
citation: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Sec. 29
text: Where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under sections 3, 5, 7 and section 9 of this Act, the Special Court shall presume, that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence, as the case may be, unless the contrary is proved by the accused.

marginal_heading: Modified Bail Provisions & Prima Facie True Standard (Watali Principle)
text: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure / BNSS, no person accused of an offence punishable under Chapters IV and VI of this Act shall, if in custody, be released on bail or on his own bond unless the Public Prosecutor has been given an opportunity of being heard. The court shall not grant bail if, on a perusal of the case diary or the report made under section 173 CrPC / 193 BNSS, the court is of the opinion that there are reasonable grounds for believing that the accusation is prima facie true (NIA v. Zahoor Ahmad Shah Watali / Vernon Gonsalves).

act_title: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
marginal_heading: Bail to a Child in Conflict with Law (Mandatory Grant)
text: When any person, who is apparently a child and is alleged to have committed a bailable or non-bailable offence, is apprehended or detained by the police, such person shall be released on bail with or without surety or placed under the supervision of a probation officer. Bail shall not be refused unless there appears reasonable grounds for believing that the release is likely to bring that person into association with any known criminal or expose the said person to moral, physical or psychological danger or the person's release would defeat the ends of justice.

act_title: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
marginal_heading: Bar on Section 438 CrPC / 482 BNSS Anticipatory Bail & Preliminary Inquiry Rule
text: Section 18 provides that nothing in Section 438 of the Code / Section 482 BNSS shall apply in relation to any case involving the arrest of any person on an accusation of having committed an offence under this Act. Section 18A(1)(a) clarifies that no preliminary inquiry shall be required for registration of an FIR, and Section 18A(1)(b) states that no approval for arrest is required. As held in Prathvi Raj Chauhan v. Union of India (2020), anticipatory bail can only be granted where no prima facie case of an offence under the Act is disclosed in the complaint.

marginal_heading: Application for Compensation before Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT)
text: An application for compensation arising out of an accident of the nature specified in sub-section (1) of section 165 may be made: (a) by the person who has sustained the injury; or (b) by the owner of the property; or (c) where death has resulted, by all or any of the legal representatives of the deceased; or (d) by any agent duly authorized. Under sub-section (3) introduced by the 2019 Amendment, no application for compensation shall be entertained unless it is made within six months of the occurrence of the accident.
